mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) signals strong household demand for housing, which correlates with elevated consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where HOUST increases by at least 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that reduces liquidity in financial markets, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months following two consecutive months with FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a strong labor market and rising consumer demand, which together drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE falls by at least 0.2pp and RSAFS rises by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A rising Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% annualized signals persistent inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where CPIAUCSL rises above 3.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.0% for three consecutive months, it indicates a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months following three consecutive months with UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising Gross Domestic Product (GDPC1) growth rate, measured quarterly, indicates expanding economic activity that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2.0% annualized.

mechanism_narrative: When residential construction starts (HOUST) fall below 650,000 units for two consecutive months, it signals a cooling housing market that reduces consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the months following two consecutive months with HOUST < 650.0.
